manual_review.batch_parameters: Each exact 64/8/1 tier overwrites every side/value/ordinal parameter; SQLite SQL parameter indexing is one based. Ordinal remains checked i64 and same source-row order. rusqlite 0.40.1 raw_execute implementation steps then resets; complete rebinding prevents stale values.
manual_review.bounds: Pending <=64 rows and sum of serialized String lengths <=65536; a larger otherwise legal row flushes pending and uses original single-row path. Pending is an allowance, not a process-RSS claim; current row and SQLite bound value copies are separate bounded storage. All prior admitted row/table/canonical/scratch limits and scale-capacity entry unchanged.
manual_review.comparison: Original projected canonical strings, source snapshots, all 15 tables, binary ordering, duplicate-preserving ordinal key, parsed Value equality including signed zero, and digests all unchanged. No equality derived from only hashes.
manual_review.failure: Every prepare/bind/execute/flush error propagates before a comparison report. Final flush must succeed before transaction commit; partial or failed scratch never yields equality and is owned by disposable directory. journal_mode=OFF does not guarantee physical rollback after spill/disk faults; no scratch reuse is introduced.
manual_review.tests_reviewed: Four new unit tests cover tier/byte boundaries, non-ASCII/NUL/escaped/blob/numeric/duplicate projections versus original spool, exact ordinal coverage, actual statement tiers, independent budget errors and SQLite full failure; two preexisting units and full integration inputs unchanged.

limitations: No Rust compilation, unit, integration, Clippy, or product/performance run performed by this review. Existing author Python SQLite control is not Rust execution.

Batching defers SQLite writes. If a pending row would fail physically and a later source row hits a budget first, the first error kind and internal failed canonical-byte count can differ from original per-row execution. Source-row budget-check relative order and immediate propagation of encountered SQL errors remain intact; separate-fault compatibility tests do not prove competing-fault precedence.
No end-to-end speedup or scale acceptance asserted; actual compiled controls and full scale acceptance remain required.
output_storage: owned /dev/shm only; no root-volume writes, no source mutations, no Cargo or product loads
